X-ray of the ecosystem: systemic loose ends, health and maturity.

```text
The ecosystem's health validator (QUALITY §5.2) — the GLOBAL view.
Unlike check (node against gate, incremental), doctor sweeps the map + the
Structure + the disk and hunts the SYSTEMIC loose ends no local gate sees:
map integrity (dead edges, phantom nodes), orphans (code without spec,
missing identity), loose layers, and gate coverage holes.

It PRESENTS and RECORDS, but does NOT block — it is diagnosis, run on demand.

With --fix, it creates what is missing: pipelines, git hooks, state labels and the
protection of the integration branch. It is IDEMPOTENT — in an already assembled
repository it changes nothing, and each repair checks before acting. Run it without asking
for authorization: it is the environment preparation step, not a project
change.
```

## Uso

```bash
anchors doctor [flags]
```

## Flags

| Flag | Padrão | O que faz |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--check-pipelines` |  | exits with 1 if any Anchors pipeline is out of date (so CI can self-verify) |
| `--fix` |  | creates what is missing in the `github` mode environment (pipelines, labels, branch protection). IDEMPOTENT: in an already set-up repository it changes nothing, and it is safe to always run |
| `--map` |  | path to the map |
| `--root` | `.` | project root |

## Saúde do projeto — família

Comandos da mesma família — o que distingue cada um:

| Comando | O que faz |
| --- | --- |
| **`anchors doctor`** | X-ray of the ecosystem: systemic loose ends, health and maturity |
| [`anchors audit`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/audit/) | Dossier of one file's pending items (gates + doctor), for batch fixing |
| [`anchors status`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/status/) | Where the project stands in the cycle, and what the next step is |
| [`anchors task-status`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/task-status/) | The round's report: what is delivered, what remains, and what comes next |
| [`anchors compliance`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/compliance/) | The state of each regulatory duty: how many nodes subject, how many comply |
| [`anchors governs`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/governs/) | Show who each guide governs (and how many) — sizes the audit per guide |

Enquanto o `check` avalia gates pontuais, o `anchors doctor` fornece um **raio-X global de todo o ecossistema**.

---

## 1. Executando `anchors doctor`

```bash
# Roda diagnóstico de saúde padrão
anchors doctor

# Roda com detalhamento diagnóstico completo
anchors doctor --verbose
```

### O que o `doctor` Detecta:
1. **Artefatos Órfãos**: Specs sem código implementado ou testes que verificam regras já deletadas.
2. **Colisão de Códigos de Identidade**: Códigos duplicados (ex: `AUTH-B01`) declarados em dois arquivos diferentes.
3. **Deriva Arquitetural**: Divergências entre as fronteiras de camadas declaradas em `anchors.yaml` e as importações reais.
4. **Buracos de Cobertura**: Camadas regidas que caíram abaixo do nível de maturidade exigido.

---

## 2. Auditoria Pontual com `anchors audit`

Quando um arquivo ou módulo específico falha em vários gates, use o `audit` para gerar a lista de correção:

```bash
anchors audit src/services/billing/invoice.spec.md
```

Ele gera um dossiê unificado com cada cenário ausente, asserção quebrada, dependência obsoleta e violação de camada daquela unidade.
